es: Reconocer las partes de un informe sobre hábitos de sueño y el marcador que introduce cada una, con tono objetivo.

teaching.en: The aim of this report is to examine the sleep habits of secondary students, and the introduction must set out the scope of the study.
teaching.es: El objetivo de este informe es examinar los hábitos de sueño de los estudiantes de secundaria, y la introducción debe exponer el alcance del estudio.
teaching.explanationEs: The aim of this report is to + verbo base es el marcador típico de la introducción; scope es lo que el estudio cubre y lo que no.
segments: The aim of this report is to examine the sleep habits of secondary
students, and the introduction must set out the scope of the study.
teaching.audioText: The aim of this report is to examine the sleep habits of secondary students, and the introduction must set out the scope of the study.

teaching.en: The method section explains how the researchers chose to carry out an online survey, in which every respondent answered ten questions.
teaching.es: La sección de método explica cómo decidieron los investigadores llevar a cabo una encuesta en línea, en la que cada encuestado respondió diez preguntas.
teaching.explanationEs: Carry out es el verbo habitual para realizar una encuesta o un estudio; respondent es la persona que contesta una encuesta.
segments: The method section explains how the researchers chose to carry out
an online survey, in which every respondent answered ten questions.
teaching.audioText: The method section explains how the researchers chose to carry out an online survey, in which every respondent answered ten questions.

teaching.en: The main findings show that 62 percent of students sleep less than eight hours, and this section reports the data without any comment.
teaching.es: Los principales resultados muestran que el 62 % de los estudiantes duerme menos de ocho horas, y esta sección presenta los datos sin ningún comentario.
teaching.explanationEs: Findings es plural: lleva show, no shows. Esta parte da los datos sin opinar.
segments: The main findings show that 62 percent of students sleep less than
eight hours, and this section reports the data without any comment.
teaching.audioText: The main findings show that 62 percent of students sleep less than eight hours, and this section reports the data without any comment.

teaching.en: The conclusion is that late screen use may affect sleep, although the sample is small and the report stays impartial about the cause.
teaching.es: La conclusión es que el uso de pantallas por la noche puede afectar al sueño, aunque la muestra es pequeña y el informe se mantiene imparcial sobre la causa.
teaching.explanationEs: La conclusión interpreta los resultados con prudencia (may) y reconoce un límite; impartial = sin tomar partido.
segments: The conclusion is that late screen use may affect sleep, although the
sample is small and the report stays impartial about the cause.
teaching.audioText: The conclusion is that late screen use may affect sleep, although the sample is small and the report stays impartial about the cause.

teaching.en: The report makes one recommendation: schools should start classes a little later, and this advice follows directly from the findings.
teaching.es: El informe hace una recomendación: los colegios deberían empezar las clases un poco más tarde, y este consejo se deriva directamente de los resultados.
teaching.explanationEs: La recomendación dice qué hacer a partir de la conclusión; suele llevar should o it is recommended that.
segments: The report makes one recommendation: schools should start classes a
little later, and this advice follows directly from the findings.
teaching.audioText: The report makes one recommendation: schools should start classes a little later, and this advice follows directly from the findings.

teaching.en: The summary at the start of a report gives a busy reader the aim, the key finding and the main recommendation in just four sentences.
teaching.es: El resumen al comienzo de un informe da a un lector ocupado el objetivo, el hallazgo clave y la recomendación principal en solo cuatro frases.
teaching.explanationEs: Summary resume todo el informe y se escribe al final, aunque se coloque al principio.
segments: The summary at the start of a report gives a busy reader the
aim, the key finding and the main recommendation in just four sentences.
teaching.audioText: The summary at the start of a report gives a busy reader the aim, the key finding and the main recommendation in just four sentences.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento y elige a qué sección del informe pertenece.

choices.text: Method: it explains how the data were gathered.
Findings: it reports what the survey showed.
Introduction: it says why the report was written.

feedback.es: El fragmento cuenta cómo se recogieron los datos (en línea, en marzo, con diez preguntas): es la sección de método.

hint.es: Fíjate en si el texto explica cómo se recogieron los datos o qué salió.

origin.text: Data were collected through an online survey in March. A total of 120 students answered ten questions about their sleep and their use of screens during the first week of the month.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo de este informe es examinar cuánto duermen los estudiantes.»

feedback.es: The aim of this report is to + verbo es el marcador clásico de una introducción: dice para qué se escribió el informe.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo que dice para qué se escribió el informe.

origin.text: Every report begins by saying why it was written. The ___ of this report is to examine how much sleep secondary students get, and the next section explains how the data were collected.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los principales resultados muestran que el 62 % duerme menos de ocho horas.»

answer.text: The main findings show that 62 percent sleep less than eight hours

feedback.es: Findings es plural y lleva show; that introduce el dato principal de la sección de resultados.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto plural: los principales resultados.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige en qué parte del informe se interpretan los datos.

choices.text: In the recommendation, which explains what the data mean.
In the conclusion, after the findings have been presented.
In the findings, where each figure is commented on.

feedback.es: La presentadora dice que los resultados se presentan sin comentario y que solo la conclusión interpreta los datos.

origin.audio: Let me talk you through a typical short report. It begins with a summary, so that a busy reader can get the key point in seconds. Then the introduction sets out the aim and the scope. The method explains how the survey was carried out, and the findings present the data without comment. Only the conclusion interprets them, and the recommendation says what should happen next.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada marcador de un informe con la sección que introduce.

pairs: The aim of this report is to…
The method was an online survey.

pairs.es: Método: cómo se recogieron los datos

pairs: The main findings show that…

pairs.es: Resultados: qué salió de los datos

pairs: It is recommended that schools…

feedback.es: Cada marcador anuncia una sección distinta del informe: objetivo, método, resultados y recomendación.

pairs: The aim of this report is to…
The method was an online survey.

pairs.es: Método: cómo se recogieron los datos

pairs: The main findings show that…

pairs.es: Resultados: qué salió de los datos

prompt.es: Mia edita una sección de resultados. Elige la frase que mantiene un tono objetivo.

choices.text: Sadly, it is shocking that most students sleep so little, and schools must act.
I believe these findings prove that students are careless about their sleep habits.
The survey shows that 62 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours.

feedback.es: Un apartado de resultados da cifras y fuente; las otras frases añaden valoraciones personales (sadly, I believe).

origin.text: Mia is editing the findings section of her report on sleep habits. The teacher has asked her to keep an impartial, neutral tone and to leave any personal comment out. She is choosing between three sentences for the first line.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la profesora del borrador en conjunto.

choices.text: That it is promising, but two sections need to be revised.
That it is well written, but the survey should have been larger.
That it is nearly ready, since only the tone of the recommendation needs changing.

feedback.es: La profesora alaba la estructura y la recomendación, pero pide corregir dos puntos: falta el método y los resultados opinan.

origin.audio: Thank you for sending your draft on student sleep. The structure is clear: you open with a summary and then state your aim. However, your method section is missing, so readers cannot tell how many students answered, or how the survey was carried out. Also, your findings section slips into opinion, with phrases like I think and sadly. A report should keep an impartial tone and save interpretation for the conclusion. Fix those two points, and the recommendation, which is already well written, will be much more convincing.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige por qué pide quitar «I think» y «sadly».

choices.text: Because those phrases are too informal for any part of a report.
Because a findings section should stay impartial and leave interpretation for later.
Because they make the recommendation sound weaker than it is.

feedback.es: La profesora dice que el informe debe mantener un tono imparcial y dejar la interpretación para la conclusión.

origin.audio: Thank you for sending your draft on student sleep. The structure is clear: you open with a summary and then state your aim. However, your method section is missing, so readers cannot tell how many students answered, or how the survey was carried out. Also, your findings section slips into opinion, with phrases like I think and sadly. A report should keep an impartial tone and save interpretation for the conclusion. Fix those two points, and the recommendation, which is already well written, will be much more convincing.

prompt.es: Completa: «120 encuestados completaron la encuesta; veinte dejaron preguntas en blanco.»

feedback.es: Respondents son las personas que contestan una encuesta; el informe indica cuántos fueron y cuántos dejaron respuestas vacías.

origin.text: A total of 120 ___ completed the survey, although twenty of them left several questions blank. The results below are based on the answers that were complete.

prompt.es: Lee las cuatro frases y elige el orden en que aparecen en un informe.

choices.text: B, C, D, A
D, B, C, A
B, D, C, A

feedback.es: El orden habitual es objetivo (B), método (D), resultados (C) y recomendación al final (A).

origin.text: A: 'It is recommended that schools start classes later.' B: 'The aim of this report is to examine student sleep.' C: 'The main findings show that 62 percent sleep under eight hours.' D: 'Data were collected through an online survey of 120 students.'

prompt.es: Elige qué problema tiene este fragmento para un informe.

choices.text: It mixes facts with personal judgement, which breaks a neutral tone.
It draws its conclusion before it has stated the aim of the study.
It is written in a tone that is too formal for a report.

feedback.es: El fragmento da un dato (la mayoría revisa mensajes), pero lo adorna con juicios (regrettably, clearly unacceptable) impropios de un informe.

origin.text: Extract from a draft: 'This report examines how students use their phones at night. Regrettably, most respondents admit that they check their messages after midnight, which is clearly unacceptable.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué la recomendación va al final del informe.

choices.text: Because readers usually skip the last part of a report.
Because it builds on the conclusion, which has to be reached first.
Because it summarises the findings for busy readers.

feedback.es: El hablante dice que la recomendación depende de la conclusión, por eso va después.

origin.audio: Two students are planning their report. One of them says: Begin with the aim, then the method. Put the recommendation last, since it depends on the conclusion that comes before it. And remember that the findings are for facts: if you want to add a comment, wait until the conclusion.

prompt.es: Completa: «El informe tenía cuarenta páginas, así que la directora leyó solo el resumen.»

feedback.es: El resumen condensa objetivo y resultado principal para quien no va a leer el informe completo.

origin.text: The report has forty pages, so the manager read only the ___ on the first page, which gave her the aim and the main result.

es: Matizar hallazgos rotundos con estructuras impersonales: there is some evidence that, it appears that, it remains unclear whether, to some extent.

teaching.en: It remains unclear whether the new timetable improves sleep, because the evidence so far is not conclusive and covers only one school.
teaching.es: Sigue sin estar claro si el nuevo horario mejora el sueño, porque las pruebas hasta ahora no son concluyentes y cubren un solo colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: It remains unclear whether + cláusula: todavía no hay respuesta. Con la duda se usa whether, no that.
segments: It remains unclear whether the new timetable improves sleep, because the
evidence so far is not conclusive and covers only one school.
teaching.audioText: It remains unclear whether the new timetable improves sleep, because the evidence so far is not conclusive and covers only one school.

teaching.en: There is some tentative evidence that longer sleep improves concentration, but the studies are small, so a degree of caution is needed.
teaching.es: Hay algunas pruebas provisionales de que dormir más mejora la concentración, pero los estudios son pequeños, así que hace falta cierta cautela.
teaching.explanationEs: There is some evidence that… admite que hay datos, pero débiles. Evidence es incontable: no lleva -s.
segments: There is some tentative evidence that longer sleep improves concentration, but
the studies are small, so a degree of caution is needed.
teaching.audioText: There is some tentative evidence that longer sleep improves concentration, but the studies are small, so a degree of caution is needed.

teaching.en: To a certain extent, the results are explained by the later start of lessons, although they are largely based on what students said.
teaching.es: Hasta cierto punto, los resultados se explican por el inicio más tardío de las clases, aunque se basan en gran medida en lo que dijeron los estudiantes.
teaching.explanationEs: To a certain extent (o to some extent) limita el alcance de la afirmación; largely reduce la fuerza de la base de datos.
segments: To a certain extent, the results are explained by the later start
of lessons, although they are largely based on what students said.
teaching.audioText: To a certain extent, the results are explained by the later start of lessons, although they are largely based on what students said.

teaching.en: It appears that screen time affects sleep, but a small sample could easily call into question a result that looks convincing at first.
teaching.es: Parece que el tiempo de pantalla afecta al sueño, pero una muestra pequeña podría poner en duda fácilmente un resultado que al principio resulta convincente.
teaching.explanationEs: It appears that… introduce una inferencia prudente; call into question significa poner en duda.
segments: It appears that screen time affects sleep, but a small sample could
easily call into question a result that looks convincing at first.
teaching.audioText: It appears that screen time affects sleep, but a small sample could easily call into question a result that looks convincing at first.

teaching.en: The data indicate that most students sleep too little, but the sample was somewhat small, so the authors ask readers to interpret it carefully.
teaching.es: Los datos indican que la mayoría de los estudiantes duerme muy poco, pero la muestra era algo pequeña, así que los autores piden a los lectores que la interpreten con cuidado.
teaching.explanationEs: Indicate es más fuerte que appears; somewhat suaviza una crítica al método.
segments: The data indicate that most students sleep too little, but the sample
was somewhat small, so the authors ask readers to interpret it carefully.
teaching.audioText: The data indicate that most students sleep too little, but the sample was somewhat small, so the authors ask readers to interpret it carefully.

teaching.en: Headlines such as 'Screens ruin sleep' are much too strong, so a careful report turns them into statements that match the evidence.
teaching.es: Titulares como «Las pantallas arruinan el sueño» son demasiado fuertes, así que un informe cuidadoso los convierte en enunciados que se ajustan a las pruebas.
teaching.explanationEs: Ruin es un verbo rotundo; el informe lo sustituye por estructuras matizadas como there is some evidence that…
segments: Headlines such as 'Screens ruin sleep' are much too strong, so
a careful report turns them into statements that match the evidence.
teaching.audioText: Headlines such as 'Screens ruin sleep' are much too strong, so a careful report turns them into statements that match the evidence.

prompt.es: Elige la reformulación que ajusta el grado de certeza a los datos de la encuesta.

choices.text: It is clear that late screen use is the reason why students sleep less.
There is some evidence that late screen use may be linked to shorter sleep.
It remains unclear whether late screen use has any link with how long students sleep.

feedback.es: La encuesta solo halló un vínculo en un colegio: There is some evidence that… y may admiten esa base débil sin afirmar una causa.

hint.es: El estudio solo halló un vínculo en un colegio: busca la estructura que admite una prueba débil.

origin.text: Draft finding: 'Late screen use ruins students' sleep.' However, the survey of 120 students only found that those who use screens late sleep less. It did not measure the reason, and it covered one school.

prompt.es: Completa: «Aún no está claro si el nuevo horario mejora el sueño.»

feedback.es: Tras unclear se introduce la duda con whether (o if), no con that.

hint.es: Es la conjunción que introduce una duda entre dos posibilidades: sí o no.

origin.text: The study has only just started and the first results are not yet available. It remains unclear ___ the new timetable improves sleep.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hasta cierto punto, los resultados se explican por el inicio más tardío.»

answer.text: To a certain extent the results are explained by the later start

feedback.es: To a certain extent limita el alcance: el inicio más tardío explica solo una parte de los resultados.

hint.es: Empieza por el matizador que significa «hasta cierto punto».

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué concluye la investigadora sobre el cambio de horario.

choices.text: That later lessons improve concentration, so every school should start later.
That the effect has been confirmed in one school over a whole year.
That more research is needed before schools change their timetables.

feedback.es: La investigadora admite que solo hay indicios débiles y pide un estudio mayor antes de cambiar horarios.

origin.audio: A researcher is summing up her study for the school newspaper. There is some tentative evidence that students who start lessons later concentrate better, but she is careful. Only one school took part, and the survey was somewhat limited. It remains unclear whether the effect would last over a whole year. She therefore calls for a larger study before any school changes its timetable.

prompt.es: Reescribe con matiz: «Homework ruins students' free time.»

answer.text: There is some evidence that homework may reduce students' free time, although it remains unclear how much.
accepted: There is some evidence that homework may reduce students' free time, although it remains unclear how much.
There is some evidence that homework can reduce students' free time, but it is unclear how large the effect is.
There is some evidence that homework tends to reduce students' free time, although the survey was somewhat limited.

feedback.es: La frase lleva There is some evidence that… más una segunda cautela (may, tends to, it remains unclear) y evita el verbo rotundo ruin.

origin.text: Hallazgo rotundo: «Homework ruins students' free time.» Reescríbelo para un informe con There is some evidence that… y una segunda cautela (may, it remains unclear…).

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué critica exactamente el lector del informe.

choices.text: That the headline is stronger than the findings below it.
That the findings section contains figures that are wrong.
That the authors have hidden the size of the effect.

feedback.es: El lector acepta los resultados del informe, pero critica que el titular sea más rotundo que lo que los datos permiten.

origin.audio: The school's sleep report has been praised, but one reader wrote in with a criticism. According to his letter, the authors wrote in their headline that screens ruin sleep, yet their own findings section says something much weaker: it appears that screen use may be linked to shorter sleep, and it remains unclear whether the effect is large. The reader does not accuse the authors of lying. He simply thinks that a headline should match the evidence below it, and that a careful report would have said there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige cómo habría redactado el lector el titular.

choices.text: With a stronger verb, since the data come from a survey.
With a cautious hedge, such as there is some evidence that.
With a question that lets readers decide for themselves.

feedback.es: El lector sugiere que un informe cuidadoso habría dicho there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.

origin.audio: The school's sleep report has been praised, but one reader wrote in with a criticism. According to his letter, the authors wrote in their headline that screens ruin sleep, yet their own findings section says something much weaker: it appears that screen use may be linked to shorter sleep, and it remains unclear whether the effect is large. The reader does not accuse the authors of lying. He simply thinks that a headline should match the evidence below it, and that a careful report would have said there is some evidence that screens affect sleep.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los resultados dependen en gran medida de cómo respondió ese grupo.»

feedback.es: Largely indica que los resultados dependen, en su mayor parte, de las respuestas de un solo grupo pequeño.

origin.text: Nearly all the data come from one group of students, so the findings depend ___ on how that group answered. A wider study would be needed to confirm them.

prompt.es: Reescribe el hallazgo con «It appears that» y una cautela más.

answer.text: It appears that students who eat breakfast tend to get better grades, although it remains unclear whether breakfast is the cause.
accepted: It appears that students who eat breakfast tend to get better grades, although it remains unclear whether breakfast is the cause.
It appears that students who have breakfast may get better grades, but it is unclear whether breakfast explains the difference.
It appears that students who eat breakfast tend to get better grades, although the evidence is not conclusive.

feedback.es: It appears that… introduce el hallazgo con prudencia y la segunda cautela (tend to, it remains unclear whether, not conclusive) evita afirmar una causa.

origin.text: Hallazgo rotundo: «Students who eat breakfast get better grades.» Reescríbelo para un informe con It appears that… y una cautela adicional (tend to, it remains unclear whether…).

prompt.es: Lee el párrafo y elige qué afirmación se formula con más certeza.

choices.text: A later start would probably change how much students sleep.
The answer may depend on how students spend their evenings.
Most students sleep too little, according to the data.

feedback.es: The data indicate… es la fórmula más firme del párrafo; it remains unclear y may marcan dudas sobre el efecto del horario.

origin.text: Extract from a report: 'The data indicate that seventy percent of students sleep too little. It remains unclear whether a later start would change that, and to a certain extent the answer may depend on how students spend their evenings.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le pide la tutora a la estudiante.

choices.text: To replace a firm claim with a more careful one.
To add more figures about the loans in the library.
To explain why the library has become so popular.

feedback.es: La tutora propone sustituir proves por una fórmula prudente, porque los préstamos no demuestran que se lea más.

origin.audio: My tutor returned my essay with a comment: you write that the new library proves that students read more. The figures only indicate a rise in loans, and it remains unclear whether people actually read the books. She suggested this instead: there is some evidence that loans have risen, which may reflect more reading.

prompt.es: Completa: «La encuesta fue algo limitada, así que los resultados son provisionales.»

feedback.es: Somewhat suaviza la crítica: la encuesta tiene límites, pero no se descarta por completo.

origin.text: The survey was ___ limited, though not useless, so the authors describe their findings as tentative rather than final. They also say that more data are needed.

es: Clasificar enunciados de un informe como hecho, inferencia u opinión según su formulación y señalar la pista lingüística.

teaching.en: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.
teaching.es: Es un hecho que el 62 % de los estudiantes duerme menos de ocho horas, y el informe nombra su fuente para que los lectores puedan comprobar la cifra.
teaching.explanationEs: Fact: algo que se puede comprobar, con cifras o fuente. En inglés es obligatorio el sujeto it en It is a fact that…
segments: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight
hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.
teaching.audioText: It is a fact that 62 percent of the students sleep less than eight hours, and the report names its source so that readers can check the figure.

teaching.en: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference, not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.
teaching.es: Podemos suponer que el colegio redujo las tareas, pero eso es una inferencia, no un hecho, y necesitaríamos los registros del colegio para confirmarlo.
teaching.explanationEs: Una inferencia se deduce de los hechos; assume y suggest son pistas de que no está comprobada.
segments: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference,
not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.
teaching.audioText: We can assume that the school cut homework, but that is an inference, not a fact, and we would need the school's records to confirm it.

teaching.en: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.
teaching.es: Si las tareas deberían ser más cortas es cuestión de opinión, y por desgracia nadie preguntó a los estudiantes qué piensan al respecto.
teaching.explanationEs: A matter of opinion: no se puede comprobar. In my opinion, should y unfortunately son pistas de opinión: valoran en lugar de comprobar.
segments: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and
unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.
teaching.audioText: Whether homework should be shorter is a matter of opinion, and unfortunately nobody asked the students what they think about it.

teaching.en: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.
teaching.es: Según la enfermera del colegio, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional, que es más fiable que las historias de segunda mano del pasillo.
teaching.explanationEs: According to + persona o documento atribuye el dato; second-hand describe información que llega a través de otros. No se dice «according to me».
segments: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a
national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.
teaching.audioText: According to the school nurse, the source of the figure is a national survey, which is more reliable than second-hand stories from the corridor.

teaching.en: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.
teaching.es: Presumiblemente, el uso de pantallas por la noche explica la caída, pero eso es especulación hasta que alguien lo compruebe, así que la certeza de la afirmación es baja.
teaching.explanationEs: Presumably marca una inferencia: probable, no comprobada; speculation es una idea sin pruebas.
segments: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until
someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.
teaching.audioText: Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but that is speculation until someone tests it, so the certainty of the statement is low.

teaching.en: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.
teaching.es: Según se dice, el colegio ha reducido las tareas en un tercio, aunque no puedo confirmarlo, y las pruebas hasta ahora son solo anecdóticas y bastante subjetivas.
teaching.explanationEs: Reportedly atribuye la información a otros sin confirmarla; anecdotal y subjective describen pruebas basadas en casos sueltos o en impresiones personales.
segments: Reportedly, the school has cut homework by a third, although I cannot confirm
it, and the evidence so far is only anecdotal and rather subjective.

prompt.es: Lee el extracto y elige cómo clasificar «Presumably, late screen use explains the drop».

choices.text: Fact: the nurse states it, so it has been checked and confirmed.
Opinion: unfortunately shows that the writer is unhappy about it.
Inference: presumably marks a likely explanation that has not been tested.

feedback.es: Presumably presenta la explicación como probable pero sin comprobar: es una inferencia, no un hecho ni una opinión.

hint.es: Busca la palabra que dice que algo es probable pero no está comprobado.

origin.text: Extract from the report: 'According to the school nurse, 62 percent of students sleep fewer than eight hours. Presumably, late screen use explains the drop, but no one has tested this idea. Unfortunately, the school has done nothing about it so far.'

prompt.es: Completa: «Podemos suponer que redujeron las tareas, pero nadie lo ha probado.»

feedback.es: Assume (o presume) introduce una suposición; en un informe indica una inferencia que aún no está comprobada.

hint.es: Es el verbo que introduce algo que damos por probable, sin pruebas.

origin.text: The report says that homework is lighter this year. We can ___ that the school cut it, but nobody has proved this yet. That is an inference, not a fact.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Según la enfermera, la fuente de la cifra es una encuesta nacional.»

answer.text: According to the nurse the source of the figure is a national survey

feedback.es: According to + persona atribuye el dato y source permite comprobarlo: es la estructura típica de un hecho.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase de la lectura es una opinión y por qué.

choices.text: That the timetable is an excellent improvement, because that word expresses a personal view.
That seventy percent prefer the new timetable, because the figure has no named source.
That attendance will rise, because the writer is completely sure about the result.

feedback.es: La profesora señala que excellent es una valoración personal: por eso esa frase es una opinión. La cifra tiene fuente y la subida de asistencia es una inferencia.

origin.audio: A teacher is reading a school report aloud and commenting on it. The report says that seventy percent of students prefer the new timetable. That is a fact, she says, because the figure comes from a named survey. Then it says that the new timetable is an excellent improvement. That, she explains, is an opinion, and the word excellent gives it away. Finally, the report says that presumably attendance will rise. That is an inference, because nobody has checked it yet.

origin.audio: A journalist is checking a school press release before publishing it. The release says that attendance has reached ninety-five percent, according to the school office. That is a fact that can be checked, she notes, and she will confirm it with the office. It then says that the new canteen is the reason for the improvement. She underlines that statement: it is an inference at best, because the release gives no evidence, and she will not print it until the school provides some. Finally, the release says that all the parents are happy. She crosses that out, since nobody has asked them: in her view it is only a guess presented as a fact.

That the decision is only a rumour with no official record at all.

origin.text: A claim without a named ___ is hard to check, so careful readers treat it with care. Even a striking number means little if nobody can say where it comes from.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le reprocha principalmente la profesora a la estudiante.

That she uses too many formal connectors in every single sentence.
That her writing does not show clearly how her ideas connect.

feedback.es: La profesora critica que la estudiante usa siempre and y but, de modo que no se ve cómo se relacionan las ideas.

origin.audio: Your results section has good numbers, but the writing needs work. First, you use and and but for everything, so the reader cannot see how your ideas connect. A formal report would say furthermore to add a fact, nevertheless to contrast, and therefore to show a consequence. Second, you wrote that the national survey agrees with you, but you never named it, so I cannot check it. Finally, you say that phones cause tiredness. Your data show only a link, so it would be safer to say that it appears that phones may play a role.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué habría que cambiar en la frase sobre los celulares.

choices.text: The claim of a cause should become a cautious statement about a link.
The figure for phones should be replaced with the national one instead.
The whole sentence should be moved to the method section of the report.

feedback.es: Los datos solo muestran un vínculo: la profesora propone sustituir la causa afirmada por it appears that… may play a role.

origin.audio: Your results section has good numbers, but the writing needs work. First, you use and and but for everything, so the reader cannot see how your ideas connect. A formal report would say furthermore to add a fact, nevertheless to contrast, and therefore to show a consequence. Second, you wrote that the national survey agrees with you, but you never named it, so I cannot check it. Finally, you say that phones cause tiredness. origin.text: Sleep problems are common in every year group. ___, the highest percentage is found in the final year, where it reaches seventy percent.

prompt.es: Escribe la sección de resultados con tres conectores, una fuente y dos matices.

answer.text: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Conversely, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep fewer than eight hours. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep, albeit on a small sample. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.
accepted: The survey was completed by 150 students. The main findings show that 60 percent of respondents sleep fewer than eight hours. Furthermore, the percentage is higher in the final year, where it reaches 70 percent. Conversely, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep fewer than eight hours. Only a minority of students, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; nevertheless, this group reports the worst sleep, albeit on a small sample. It appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep, although the survey cannot prove this. These results are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers sleep too little. Therefore, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the highest figure is found in the final year. More research is needed to confirm these findings.

According to the survey of 150 students, 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours, and the figure rises to 70 percent in the final year. Moreover, only 45 percent of first-year students sleep so little. A minority of respondents, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; however, they report the worst sleep, albeit in a small group. There is some evidence that phones may affect sleep, but the data do not show that they are the cause. The findings are consistent with the national survey, which stated that teenagers do not sleep enough. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a later start. Notably, the figure is highest in the final year, and further research would be useful.

The survey of 150 students found that 60 percent sleep fewer than eight hours. In addition, the percentage rises to 70 percent in the final year, whereas it is 45 percent in the first year. A minority, 18 percent, use a phone after midnight; even so, these students report the worst sleep. It seems that late phone use may play a role, although the survey cannot prove it. According to the national survey, teenagers sleep too little, so the results are consistent with earlier research. As a result, the school may wish to consider a later start. Notably, the final year shows the highest figure, and more evidence would be welcome.

feedback.es: La sección combina cifras, tres conectores formales, una fuente y al menos dos afirmaciones matizadas (it appears that, may, tend to).

origin.text: Encuesta escolar sobre el sueño (150 estudiantes): el 60 % duerme menos de ocho horas; en último curso, el 70 %; en primer curso, el 45 %; el 18 % usa el celular después de medianoche y duerme peor. La encuesta nacional afirma que los adolescentes duermen poco. Escribe unas 125 a 200 palabras: tres conectores formales (furthermore, nevertheless, therefore…), la fuente y dos afirmaciones matizadas.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que integra la fuente nacional con prudencia.

choices.text: Our figure of 60 percent proves the national report, which is obviously right about teenagers everywhere.
Our figure of 60 percent is consistent with the national report, which stated that 55 percent sleep too little.
Our figure of 60 percent contradicts the national report, although the two numbers are in fact very close.

feedback.es: Consistent with cita la fuente sin exagerar; proves y contradicts dicen más o algo distinto de lo que muestran las dos cifras.

origin.text: You must refer to a national report that found that 55 percent of teenagers sleep under eight hours. Your own school survey found 60 percent. The two figures are close, and your sample is much smaller than theirs.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué prefiere Mia la segunda versión de la frase.

choices.text: Because it is shorter and easier to read aloud.
Because it includes figures that the first one lacks.
Because it matches what the survey actually shows.

feedback.es: Mia prefiere la segunda porque refleja un vínculo, no una causa, y un informe no debe afirmar más de lo que permiten los datos.

origin.audio: Mia is reading out two versions of a sentence. The first says that phones are the reason why students sleep badly. The second says that it appears that late phone use may be linked to poor sleep. She prefers the second one, because the survey shows a link and not a cause, and a good report should never claim more than the data allow.

feedback.es: Minority significa menos de la mitad; combina con only para dejar claro que el grupo es pequeño.

es: Elaborar un mini informe sobre el transporte escolar y presentarlo en un resumen oral de un minuto con punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

teaching.en: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.
teaching.es: En resumen, este informe ofrece una visión general de cómo hacen los estudiantes su trayecto diario al colegio, según una encuesta a cien familias.
teaching.explanationEs: In brief resume en una frase; give an overview introduce el panorama general; commute es el trayecto diario al colegio o al trabajo.
segments: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their
daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.
teaching.audioText: In brief, this report gives an overview of how students make their daily commute to school, according to a survey of one hundred families.

teaching.en: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.
teaching.es: Presentaré a grandes rasgos los principales resultados en un minuto, así que seleccionaré solo las dos o tres cifras que más importan a los oyentes.
teaching.explanationEs: I will outline… es la fórmula oral para anunciar el resumen; pick out es elegir lo más importante y dejar lo demás.
segments: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick
out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.
teaching.audioText: I will outline the main findings in one minute, so I will pick out only the two or three figures that matter most to the listeners.

teaching.en: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus, and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.
teaching.es: La idea clave es que la mayoría de los estudiantes depende del autobús escolar, y esa es la idea principal que quiero que recuerde el público.
teaching.explanationEs: The key point is that… da la idea central; en una presentación oral se dice una sola vez y se repite al final como key takeaway.
segments: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus,
and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.
teaching.audioText: The key point is that most students depend on the school bus, and that is the key takeaway I want the audience to remember.

teaching.en: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.
teaching.es: Para concluir, parece que los autobuses con retraso son el problema principal, aunque hacen falta más pruebas antes de poder estar seguros.
teaching.explanationEs: To conclude cierra el resumen; se mantiene la cautela de las clases anteriores (it appears, more evidence is needed).
segments: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem,
although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.
teaching.audioText: To conclude, it appears that late buses are the main problem, although more evidence is needed before we can be certain.

teaching.en: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the journey for the students who live furthest from the school.
teaching.es: Recomendamos un segundo autobús por la mañana, que acortaría el trayecto de los estudiantes que viven más lejos del colegio.
teaching.explanationEs: We recommend + sustantivo o -ing; el condicional would dice el efecto esperado.
segments: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the

teaching.audioText: We recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the journey for the students who live furthest from the school.

teaching.explanationEs: Un resumen oral breve elige los dos o tres datos más importantes; distil es condensar, y keep to time, no pasarse del tiempo.

prompt.es: Elige la frase que abre el informe con una visión general del tema.

This report gives an overview of how students travel to school, based on a survey of 100 students.
This report gives my own feelings about travelling to school with my friends every day.

feedback.es: Give an overview presenta el panorama general del tema y la base de datos; las otras opciones son una lista exhaustiva o una opinión personal.

origin.text: You surveyed 100 students about how they travel to school. Fifty-two come by school bus and thirty walk. Your report needs an opening sentence that gives the reader the overall picture, before any detail.

feedback.es: Concise describe un resumen breve y directo: solo lo esencial, sin repetir todo el informe.

hint.es: Es el adjetivo que describe un texto breve que dice mucho con pocas palabras.

origin.text: I have only one minute for the whole talk. To keep the summary ___, I will mention only two findings and leave the rest for the written report.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué idea cierra el resumen la oradora.

choices.text: With a warning that the evidence is too weak to justify any action.
With a summary of the two figures she has mentioned.
With a proposal that follows from the problem she found.

feedback.es: La oradora cierra con To conclude, we recommend…: una propuesta que se deriva del problema principal.

origin.audio: Good morning. I will outline the main findings of our survey on school transport in one minute. The key point is that more than half of the students depend on the school bus. It appears that late buses are the main problem, although we need more evidence. To conclude, we recommend a second morning bus, which would shorten the trip for students who live far away.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del resumen oral con su función.

feedback.es: Un buen resumen oral anuncia, da la idea central, matiza y cierra con una recomendación.

origin.audio: Your summary was clear, but it ran for almost two minutes, so you must cut it. You announced the topic well, and your key point about the school bus was memorable. However, you read out five different figures, and the audience will remember only one or two of them. Choose the two that matter most. You also sounded certain that late buses are the cause; say instead that it appears they may be the main problem. Finish with your recommendation, as you did, because it is the part that people act on.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué valora positivamente la profesora.

choices.text: The large number of figures that were included in it.
The certain tone used to describe the main cause.
The announcement of the topic and the final recommendation.

feedback.es: La profesora alaba el anuncio claro del tema y el cierre con la recomendación, que es lo que el público puede aplicar.

origin.text: Thank you all for coming. In the next minute I will briefly ___ the main findings of our survey on the commute, starting with the key point.

prompt.es: Escribe el mini informe: objetivo, método, resultados, matiz, conclusión y recomendación.

answer.text: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.
accepted: The aim of this report is to describe how students travel to school. The method was a survey of 100 students carried out by the school council, and every answer was included in the analysis. The main findings show that 52 percent of respondents come by school bus, whereas only 6 percent cycle. The remaining students either walk, 30 percent, or come by car, 12 percent. Furthermore, 35 students said that the bus journey takes more than forty minutes. It appears that long journeys may be a problem for students who live far away, although more evidence is needed. The conclusion is that the school bus is the most common way to travel. Therefore, it is recommended that the school should consider a second morning bus, which would probably shorten the daily commute. The survey was somewhat limited, so the results should be treated as tentative.

This report gives an overview of how students get to school. A survey of 100 students was carried out by the school council. The findings show that more than half of the respondents, 52 percent, use the school bus, while 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and only 6 percent cycle. In addition, 35 students said that the journey by bus takes longer than forty minutes. There is some evidence that long journeys may affect students who live far away, but it remains unclear how many are affected. To conclude, the bus is the main way to travel. We recommend that the school consider an extra bus in the morning, which would shorten the daily commute for many families.

The aim of this report is to show how students travel to school. We surveyed 100 students, and every student answered in class, so all the replies could be included. According to the survey, 52 percent travel by school bus, 30 percent walk, 12 percent come by car and 6 percent cycle. Nevertheless, the bus is not always convenient: 35 students said that the journey takes over forty minutes. It seems that this may be a problem for those who live far away, although the survey cannot prove it. Therefore, we recommend a second morning bus. The conclusion is that the school bus is essential, and a second one could improve the daily commute for many students.

prompt.es: Lee el borrador y elige qué debería mejorar el resumen oral.

choices.text: It lists too many figures and lacks a clear key point.
It sounds too informal and includes too many personal opinions.
It should have started with the recommendation instead of the figures.

feedback.es: El borrador enumera cinco cifras seguidas sin decir cuál importa: falta una idea clave que el público pueda recordar.

origin.text: Draft of a one-minute summary: 'Our survey asked 100 students about transport. We found that 52 came by bus, 30 walked, 12 came by car and 6 cycled. Also 35 said that the bus takes more than forty minutes, 22 said that it is sometimes late and 14 said that it is crowded.'

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué repetirá la estudiante la idea clave al final.

choices.text: Because the written report did not include that point.
Because listeners cannot go back and read it again.
Because she has to fill the whole minute with something.

feedback.es: Al no poder releer, el oyente necesita que la idea central se repita al final.

origin.audio: A student is comparing her written report with her oral summary. The report has a method section and a long list of findings. In the talk she will skip the method and mention only two findings, because the listeners cannot read the tables. She will repeat the key point at the end, so nobody forgets it.

prompt.es: Escribe el resumen oral de un minuto con anuncio, punto clave, cautela y recomendación.

answer.text: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.
accepted: I will outline the main findings of our survey on digital habits. The key point is that 64 of the 80 students use a phone for more than three hours a day. Only a minority, 20 students, sleep fewer than seven hours. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. To conclude, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

I will briefly present our survey on digital habits. The main point is that most students, 64 out of 80, use a phone for more than three hours daily. It seems that heavy users may sleep less, but we cannot be sure. Only 20 students sleep fewer than seven hours. In conclusion, we recommend one hour without phones before bed.

I will give an overview of our digital habits survey. The key finding is that 64 of our 80 students use a phone for over three hours a day. It appears that heavy users tend to sleep less, although more evidence is needed. In short, we recommend a phone-free hour before bed.

feedback.es: El resumen anuncia, da el punto clave con una cifra, añade una cautela y cierra con una recomendación, en frases cortas.

origin.text: Encuesta sobre hábitos digitales (80 estudiantes): 64 usan el celular más de tres horas al día; solo 20 duermen menos de siete horas; los que más lo usan parecen dormir menos.
